papers.title: Exposure-informed lung transcriptomic analysis links predicted NNK targets to cell type-specific remodeling programs in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is associated with cigarette smoking, yet the relationship between the tobacco-specific nitrosamine nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) and IPF-associated lung transcriptional remodeling remains incompletely understood. Here, we developed an exposure-informed computational framework integrating multi-database target prediction, lung single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis, co-expression network analysis, bulk lung cohort projection, and exploratory structure-based modeling. Putative human protein targets of NNK were predicted from ChEMBL
papers.summary: This study presents a computational framework integrating target prediction, single-cell transcriptomics, and network analysis to link the tobacco-specific nitrosamine NNK to cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The findings suggest that NNK may influence specific lung cell types and gene networks relevant to IPF pathology, providing a potential mechanistic link between smoking and IPF progression.

papers.title: Probing pyrazolo-pyrimidines as SIRT2 inhibitors via molecular modelling and biological assays.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) involvement in different biological pathways opens a promising scenario for the development of related ligands to be evaluated as therapeutic agents in different diseases, such as cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, cardiovascular and autoimmune diseases. The continuous elucidation of several SIRT2-ligand complexes fostered the discovery of novel and more selective SIRT2 inhibitors (SIRT2Is). Among them, SIRT2 in the presence of SirReal2 analogues was the most investigated. We recently reported pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds (1-5) as SIRT2Is (1, SIRT2 % inhibition =
papers.summary: This study investigates pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds as selective inhibitors of SIRT2, an enzyme implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, using molecular modeling and biological assays. The findings identify promising lead compounds with improved selectivity and potency, providing a foundation for further therapeutic development.

papers.title: Behind substrate specificity switch in lactate dehydrogenase: Active-site loop dynamics and epistatic enhancement.
papers.abstract: Substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) controls metabolic flux and remains a central challenge in enzyme engineering, particularly when closely related substrates differ by only a single carboxylate group. Although Q102 (equivalent to Gln86 in Geobacillus stearothermophilus L-LDH) is recognized as a canonical substrate-specificity determinant, how this electrostatic switch cooperates with steric effects, conformational dynamics, and scaffold context to govern substrate recognition remains unclear. Here, we combined steady-state kinetics with molecular dynamics simulations to ex
papers.summary: This study investigates how substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenases is controlled by an active-site loop, revealing that a canonical electrostatic switch (Q102) cooperates with steric effects and conformational dynamics. Using kinetics and molecular dynamics, the authors show that epistatic interactions with the scaffold context enhance the specificity switch, providing a more complete model for enzyme engineering.

papers.title: Quantifying protein unfolding kinetics with a high-throughput microfluidic platform.
papers.abstract: Even after folding, proteins sample unfolded intermediates at risk of irreversible alteration (e.g., via proteolysis, aggregation, or posttranslational modification). Thus, kinetic stability impacts protein lifetime and abundance. However, we have very few measurements of unfolding rates, largely due to technical challenges. To address this, we developed SPARKfold (simultaneous proteolysis assay revealing kinetics of folding), a microfluidic platform to express, purify, and measure unfolding rate constants at high throughput via native proteolysis. We applied SPARKfold to determine unfolding r
papers.summary: The authors developed SPARKfold, a high-throughput microfluidic platform that expresses, purifies, and measures protein unfolding rate constants via native proteolysis. This addresses the technical challenge of measuring kinetic stability, which is important for understanding protein lifetime and abundance. The platform enables large-scale quantification of unfolding kinetics, filling a critical gap in protein biophysics.

papers.title: Three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction by atomic force microscopy imaging and template matching allows rapid structural-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image.
papers.abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is a versatile multi-modal imaging method frequently used for structural characterisation of biological surfaces at the nanoscale. However, AFM-based three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction has hitherto not been possible due to the tip-sample convolution artifact that distorts AFM images of individual molecules, and the disconnect between two-dimensional AFM images of surface deposited molecules and their three-dimensional structures. Here, three-dimensional single-particle analysis was developed for rapid structure-based validation of protein structures
papers.summary: This paper presents a new method for three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction using atomic force microscopy (AFM) combined with template matching, overcoming the tip-sample convolution artifact that previously limited AFM structural analysis. The approach enables rapid structure-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image, providing a fast and accessible alternative for protein structural verification.

papers.title: Multivalent ion binding site identification with structure-based deep learning.
papers.abstract: Protein-ion interactions are essential for many cellular processes, including enzymatic catalysis, signaling, and allosteric regulation. However, mapping ion-binding sites experimentally remains labor-intensive and expensive. Here, we present BiteNetI, a structure-based deep learning model that uses 3D convolutional neural networks to simultaneously localize ion-binding centers and predict binding residues for 14 biologically relevant ions. Trained on a carefully curated dataset of over 10,000 high-resolution protein-ion complexes, in which near-identical binding sites are consistently annotat
papers.summary: BiteNetI is a new deep learning tool that predicts where 14 different biologically relevant ions bind to proteins directly from their 3D structure, identifying both the binding center and the interacting residues. Trained on a large curated dataset of over 10,000 protein-ion complexes, it offers a fast, cost-effective alternative to experimental ion-binding site mapping and could help researchers studying catalysis, signaling, and regulation.

papers.title: Development of the First YTHDC1 Degrader with Improved Antileukemia Activity.
papers.abstract: N6-Methyladenosine (m6A) represents the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic mRNA, with YTHDC1 serving as a critical nuclear reader protein implicated in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although selective inhibitors of YTHDC1 have been reported, whether targeted degradation of YTHDC1 could achieve enhanced therapeutic efficacy remains unexplored. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of the first PROTAC molecule targeting YTHDC1, termed XY-2, which was developed based on the cocrystal structure of YTHDC1 bound to its known inhibitor. XY-2 efficiently induced proteas
papers.summary: This paper reports the first PROTAC degrader (XY-2) targeting the m6A reader protein YTHDC1, designed from a cocrystal structure with a known inhibitor. XY-2 induces proteasomal degradation of YTHDC1 and shows improved antileukemia activity compared to existing inhibitors, suggesting that targeted degradation may offer a more effective therapeutic strategy for AML.

papers.title: A Ligand-Triggered Receptor Conformation Enables the Design of Selective Agonists for the Dopamine 3 Receptor (D3R) Using a Bitopic Strategy.
papers.abstract: While G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the largest drug target family, designing subtype-selective molecules is still a challenge, especially to distinguish among closely related subtypes. One of the most challenging cases is the distinction between dopamine D2R and D3R, pivotal receptors in motor functions and cognition, and targets of Parkinson's disease treatments, schizophrenia, or substance use disorders. Attempts to design D3R-selective molecules with ligands binding toward the first transmembrane helix (the most sequence-diverse and conformationally flexible segment in GPCR
papers.summary: This study reveals a ligand-triggered conformational change in the dopamine 3 receptor (D3R) that enables the design of highly selective bitopic agonists, distinguishing D3R from the closely related D2R. By targeting the first transmembrane helix, a region of high sequence diversity, the authors achieve subtype selectivity, offering a new strategy for developing drugs with fewer side effects for conditions like Parkinson's disease and schizophrenia.

papers.title: [Enhancing the thermostability of Pseudoalteromonas sp. κ-carrageenase through computer-aided rational design].
papers.abstract: κ-carrageenan oligosaccharides hold broad application prospects in the food and pharmaceutical fields due to their excellent bioactivity. κ-carrageenase is a key enzyme for the industrial production of high-value carrageenan oligosaccharides, while the insufficient thermostability limits its application. The objective of this study is to rationally redesign the κ-carrageenase derived from Pseudoalteromonas through a computer-aided strategy, with the aim of constructing and screening enzyme variants exhibiting significantly enhanced thermostability. Discovery Studio 2019 was used for multi-site
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used computer-aided rational design to enhance the thermostability of κ-carrageenase from Pseudoalteromonas, a key enzyme for producing bioactive carrageenan oligosaccharides. By introducing targeted mutations, the authors successfully constructed enzyme variants with significantly improved thermostability, which could benefit industrial applications.

papers.title: Localized Rigidification and Allosteric Modulation Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Neutralization by Class 3 and Class 4 Antibodies at Atomic Resolution: An Integrated Computational Study of Binding, Dynamics, and Allostery.
papers.abstract: The relentless evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of highly antibody-evasive variants underscore the need to decipher the molecular principles that govern antibody neutralization breadth and resilience. In this study, we employ an integrated computational framework combining structural analysis, conformational dynamics, mutational scanning, binding energetics, and allosteric network modeling to dissect the mechanistic signatures of class 3 and class 4 antibodies targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Through comprehensive analysis of antibody-RBD co
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses an integrated computational approach to dissect how class 3 and class 4 antibodies neutralize the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, revealing that they rigidify the receptor-binding domain and modulate allosteric networks at atomic resolution. The findings provide mechanistic insights into antibody neutralization breadth and resilience against evolving variants.

papers.title: Repurposing FDA-Approved Drugs as Nav1.7 Channel Modulators: An Integrated Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.7 is a strongly validated target for the development of novel, non-opioid analgesics due to its genetic link to pain signaling. To accelerate the discovery of safe Nav1.7 modulators, this study outlines an integrated computational pipeline to repurpose FDA-approved drugs. A structurally complete model of the Nav1.7 central pore was generated via homology modeling from a high-resolution cryo-EM structure (PDB: 7W9K) to ensure a physically consistent model suitable for dynamic simulations. We conducted a structure-based virtual screening of 2296 FDA-approved
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as modulators of the Nav1.7 sodium channel, a validated target for non-opioid pain relief. By building a homology model of the channel and screening 2296 approved drugs, the authors identify potential lead compounds for further development.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology Guided Drug Repurposing and Molecular Modeling Identify Sulfasalazine as a Potential OXA-23 β-Lactamase in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii has become a major health concern, primarily driven by the dissemination of class D β-lactamases, particularly OXA-23, which compromise the efficacy of last-line β-lactam antibiotics. Drug repurposing combined with structure-based computational approaches provides a promising strategy for accelerating the discovery of novel therapeutic candidates against multidrug-resistant pathogens. This study aimed to identify FDA-approved non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) with potential inhibitory activity against OXA-23 β-lac
papers.summary: This study used network pharmacology and molecular modeling to screen FDA-approved NSAIDs for potential inhibitors of the OXA-23 β-lactamase, which is a key driver of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. They identified sulfasalazine as a promising candidate that could be repurposed to restore the efficacy of last-line β-lactam antibiotics against this multidrug-resistant pathogen.

papers.title: RNA G-quadruplex structure recognition by chimeric peptides.
papers.abstract: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical nucleic acids involved in gene regulation and have attracted interest as potential therapeutic targets. However, developing ligands that selectively recognize specific G4 structures remains challenging. Here, we report the rational design of chimeric peptides that combine a de novo selected peptide (Pep11) with a native peptide (Rhau18) derived from the endogenous DHX36 protein. The chimeric peptides bound RNA G4s (rG4s) with nanomolar affinity, representing a 10-fold enhancement over the individual modules, while retaining selectivity for rG4s over DNA G
papers.summary: The authors rationally designed chimeric peptides by combining a de novo selected peptide with a native DHX36-derived peptide, achieving nanomolar binding to RNA G-quadruplexes with 10-fold enhanced affinity over individual modules while maintaining selectivity for RNA over DNA G4s. This provides a new strategy for developing selective RNA G4 ligands with potential therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insights into Antibiotic Structure-Activity Relationships and Mechanisms of Action: A Review.
papers.abstract: This review examines recent quantum chemical methodologies applied to investigating antibiotic structure and mechanisms of action. The discussion is organised into three sections: (1) enzymatic hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring, (2) interactions of antibiotics with ribosomal subunits and enzyme active sites, and (3) complex formation with metal ions. Each section evaluates how quantum chemical approaches, particularly density functional theory (DFT) and hybrid QM/MM techniques, model molecular processes relevant to antibiotic function, including transition states, electron density analyses, and
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent quantum chemical studies on antibiotics, focusing on how DFT and QM/MM methods reveal mechanisms of β-lactam hydrolysis, ribosome binding, and metal-ion interactions. It highlights how these computational approaches provide atomic-level insights into structure-activity relationships and drug action, which could aid in designing more effective antibiotics.

papers.title: Ligand Design Using Unique Conformations to Preferentially Dock a Specific Site on Collagen-Bound MMP1.
papers.abstract: Precise site-specific ligand design remains a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery. Most existing approaches screen ligands against binding pockets identified from static protein structures obtained by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, or AlphaFold predictions. However, protein function is governed by a structure-dynamics-function relationship, and ligand screening that does not account for binding competition across the protein surface or the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent conformational states remains incomplete. Substrate-specific confo
papers.summary: This study presents a ligand design strategy that leverages unique protein conformations to achieve site-specific docking on collagen-bound MMP1, addressing the challenge of binding competition and dynamic conformational states in structure-based drug discovery. By considering substrate-dependent conformations, the approach improves selectivity for a particular site on the target protein.

papers.title: Rational Design of Novel Isosteviol-Derived Factor Xa Inhibitors Using Integrated QSAR, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA Analyses.
papers.abstract: Factor Xa (FXa) remains an important target in the development of anticoagulant and antithrombotic agents. In this study, twenty isosteviol-derived oxime ether analogs previously reported as FXa inhibitors were used to develop a predictive QSAR model. The compounds were geometry-optimized at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level, and Dragon molecular descriptors were calculated from the optimized structures. After descriptor filtering, Random Forest-based supervised preselection and correlation-based pruning were applied. Several models of increasing complexity were evaluated, including multiple linea
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (QSAR, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA) to rationally design novel isosteviol-derived inhibitors of Factor Xa, an anticoagulant target. The authors built predictive models from 20 known analogs and identified key structural features for activity, providing a basis for developing new antithrombotic agents.

papers.title: Higher-order assembly of a type IX retron enables exploitation for designer antimicrobials.
papers.abstract: Bacterial defense systems provide a rich reservoir for biotechnological innovation. Retrons are tripartite abortive infection systems that detect phage invasion using reverse-transcribed DNA (msDNA), but how they structurally couple threat detection to effector activation remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structure and activation mechanism of retron-Kva2, a type IX retron from the human pathogen Klebsiella variicola. We reveal that retron-Kva2 assembles into an asymmetric, higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic dimeric HEPN RNase at its core. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study reveals the cryo-EM structure of a type IX retron from Klebsiella variicola, showing how it assembles into a higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic HEPN RNase. The structural insights explain how threat detection is coupled to effector activation and enable the design of retron-based antimicrobials.

papers.title: Drying-Induced Structural and Oxidative Transformations in Sustainable Proteins: Impact on Physicochemical Properties and Flavor-Binding Functionality.
papers.abstract: The rapid global transition toward sustainable food systems has intensified interest in alternative protein ingredients derived from both terrestrial plants and blue foods. However, a critical bottleneck in the commercialization of these proteins is the stabilization of flavor profiles during dehydration. Drying technologies ranging from conventional hot-air and heat pump drying to microwave and vacuum freeze-drying inevitably induce structural reorganization and oxidative modifications. These transformations fundamentally modulate how volatile flavor compounds are bound, retained, and release
papers.summary: This review examines how different drying methods (hot-air, heat pump, microwave, and vacuum freeze-drying) alter the structure and oxidation state of alternative proteins from plants and blue foods, and how these changes affect flavor-binding and release. It highlights that drying-induced modifications are a critical bottleneck for stabilizing flavor profiles in sustainable protein ingredients.

papers.title: Tryptophan Residues' Incorporation Modulates Ferritin Thermal Stability and Hydrophobicity.
papers.abstract: Ferritin, a physiological iron-storage protein, has emerged as a highly attractive platform for drug delivery owing to its biocompatibility, structural robustness, and intrinsic ability to encapsulate and protect therapeutic cargo within its hollow nanocage. Building upon previous studies that established the baseline characteristics of engineered ferritin mutants in comparison to the wild-type protein, this work specifically investigates and directly compares the thermal stability profiles of two distinct mutated variants. These variants of human H-chain ferritin, obtained through targeted si
papers.summary: This study investigates how incorporating tryptophan residues into human H-chain ferritin affects its thermal stability and surface hydrophobicity, comparing two engineered mutants to the wild-type protein. The findings reveal that tryptophan incorporation modulates these properties, which could inform the design of ferritin-based drug delivery nanocages with tailored stability and cargo-loading characteristics.

papers.title: Nanozymes in the Treatment of Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases: Opportunities and Challenges.
papers.abstract: Pediatric inflammatory diseases, such as neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and asthma, pose numerous challenges in clinical treatment due to their complex pathogenesis and the still-developing stage of children's immune systems. These challenges include poor precision, strong toxic and side effects, and unclear long-term biological safety. In recent years, the development of nanozymes has provided new opportunities to address these issues. This review systematically summarizes the latest research progress of nanozymes in the diagnosis and treatment
papers.summary: This review discusses the potential of nanozymes—nanomaterials with enzyme-like activity—for treating pediatric inflammatory diseases such as necrotizing enterocolitis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and asthma. It highlights how nanozymes could improve treatment precision and reduce side effects, while also addressing the challenges of safety and clinical translation in children.

papers.title: Hierarchy of grammar rules for the language of transcriptional activation domains.
papers.abstract: Transcriptional activation domains (ADs) of eukaryotic gene activators have remained enigmatic for decades as short, consensus-less, extremely variable amino acid sequences that lack a specific structure and interact fuzzily with an uncertain number of targets. Understanding AD sequence grammar is critical for solving the enigma. Using rational design of AD sequences and high-throughput in vivo experimentation combined with bioinformatic analysis and machine learning, we refined grammar rules for AD sequences, calculated the relative importance of each rule to define a rule hierarchy, and link
papers.summary: This study decodes the sequence grammar of transcriptional activation domains (ADs), which are short, unstructured protein regions that activate gene expression. By combining rational design, high-throughput in vivo assays, bioinformatics, and machine learning, the authors define a hierarchy of grammar rules and their relative importance, providing a predictive framework for AD function.

papers.title: Stabilization of prefusion hMPV F improves manufacturability and protective immunity across hMPV lineages.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of pediatric acute lower respiratory tract infections (ALRTIs), yet vaccine development has been hindered by the intrinsic metastability of the prefusion F glycoprotein (pre-F). Here, we used a structure-based design strategy to stabilize hMPV pre-F while preserving neutralization-sensitive epitopes. By applying combined stabilizing elements, including disulfide bonds, a designed salt bridge, and a trimer-interface sequence swap, we generated VM-874, a pre-F-stabilized trimer that was expressed at high levels in 293F cells and exhibited improved th
papers.summary: This study describes a structure-based design approach to stabilize the prefusion F glycoprotein of human metapneumovirus (hMPV), yielding a variant (VM-874) with improved expression and manufacturability. The stabilized trimer preserves neutralization-sensitive epitopes and elicits protective immunity across hMPV lineages, addressing a key barrier in vaccine development.

papers.title: Deciphering the action mechanism of the sacred plant "Ashvattha" (Ficus religiosa L.) in the treatment of delayed-onset muscle soreness.
papers.abstract: DOMS is a common post-exercise syndrome characterized by pain, stiffness, and decreased muscle function. Conventional therapies have limited efficacy and have potential side effects.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This paper investigates the molecular mechanism by which the sacred plant Ashvattha (Ficus religiosa) may alleviate delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), a common post-exercise condition with limited treatment options. The study likely uses computational or experimental approaches to identify active compounds and pathways, providing a scientific basis for this traditional remedy.

papers.title: TagR, a newly identified member of the MarR family of transcriptional regulators, represses the NRPS operon in Klebsiella oxytoca.
papers.abstract: Toxigenic Klebsiella oxytoca strains produce the pyrrolobenzodiazepine enterotoxins tilimycin (TM) and tilivalline (TV), which contribute to the development of antibiotic-associated hemorrhagic colitis. The biosynthesis of these toxins depends on the nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) operon located within the til pathogenicity island. Although several global and signal-responsive regulators of NRPS operon expression have been identified, the regulatory network governing enterotoxin biosynthesis remains incompletely characterized. In this study, we identified a previously unrecognized tran
papers.summary: This study identifies TagR, a new member of the MarR family of transcriptional regulators, which represses the NRPS operon responsible for enterotoxin biosynthesis in Klebsiella oxytoca. The finding expands the known regulatory network controlling toxin production, which is linked to antibiotic-associated hemorrhagic colitis.

papers.title: Discovery of indazole-carboxamide based USP8 inhibitor for immune activation and antitumor response in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (CRC), which accounts for most CRC cases, responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Increasing evidence suggests that the deubiquitinase USP8 maintains PD-L1 protein expression by erasing its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby preserving membrane PD-L1 and facilitating immune escape. How pharmacological inhibition of USP8 regulates PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity in CRC, however, has not been fully clarified.
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel indazole-carboxamide-based inhibitor of the deubiquitinase USP8 and demonstrates that it reduces PD-L1 protein stability in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer cells, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses. The findings suggest that pharmacological USP8 inhibition could be a promising strategy to overcome resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors in this difficult-to-treat cancer subtype.

papers.title: Inhibition of amyloid β aggregation by venetoclax: a computational and in vitro experimental approach.
papers.abstract: The aggregation of amyloid β-protein (Aβ) plays a key role in the pathological progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Given the current absence of effective therapeutic strategies, the drug repurposing approach provides novel insights into the treatment of AD. Venetoclax, a B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of hematological malignancies, characterized by well-defined pharmacokinetic properties and a favorable safety profile. However, its effects and molecular mechanisms in the treatment of AD remain unexplored. Here, we investigated th
papers.summary: This study explores venetoclax, an approved cancer drug, as a potential inhibitor of amyloid beta aggregation in Alzheimer's disease using computational and in vitro experiments. The findings suggest that venetoclax may interfere with Aβ aggregation, offering a promising drug repurposing candidate for AD treatment.

papers.title: Ziziphusine A, a unique plant-alkaloid featuring amide rotational isomerism from the fruits of Ziziphus jujuba with anti-inflammatory activity.
papers.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba var. inermis Rehder (Rhamnaceae) is an edible medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine and functional foods. Phytochemical investigation of the methanolic extract of its fruits resulted in the isolation of a rare amide rotational isomeric alkaloid, ziziphusine A (1), together with eight known compounds including brassicasterol (2), (E)-24-nor-cholest-22-en-3β-ol (3), alphitolic acid (4), 3-O-cis-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (5), 3-O-trans-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (6), E-p-methoxycinnamic acid (7), (Z)-3-(4,5-dihydroxy-2-methoxyphenyl)acrylic acid (8), and scopoleti
papers.summary: Researchers isolated a rare alkaloid, ziziphusine A, from jujube fruits, notable for its amide rotational isomerism, along with eight known compounds. The compound showed anti-inflammatory activity, suggesting potential medicinal value.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomics and single-cell analysis identify SIX4 as a candidate epithelial target in ovarian cancer and PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a heterogeneous solid tumor, whereas polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a distinct endocrine-metabolic ovarian disorder. Whether PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation and ovarian cancer share convergent transcriptomic candidates remains unclear. This study aimed to identify shared transcriptomic candidates and define their cellular localization without implying a causal or clinical comorbidity relationship.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared gene expression changes between ovarian cancer and PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation, pinpointing SIX4 as a candidate epithelial target. The findings suggest convergent molecular pathways in these distinct ovarian conditions, though the authors do not imply a causal or clinical comorbidity link.

papers.title: Antibacterial Activity of α-Sulfamidophosphonate Derivatives and Their In Silico Assessment as Dihydropteroate Synthase Binders.
papers.abstract: In this study, we report the first antibacterial evaluation of a focused library of 12 previously synthesized α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives (4a-4l) against a panel of nine Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains, including ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales. The overall hit rate was modest, as most compounds were inactive at the highest tested concentration (MIC ≥ 256 µg/mL), indicating a narrow and strain-selective profile. Nevertheless, selected derivatives showed noteworthy activity against individual isolates: 4 g inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC29213 at 4 µg/mL, 4
papers.summary: This study presents the first antibacterial evaluation of 12 α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including resistant strains. Most compounds showed weak activity, but one derivative (4g) exhibited notable inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus at 4 µg/mL. In silico docking suggested these compounds may bind to dihydropteroate synthase, providing a potential mechanism for further optimization.

papers.title: Straightforward Synthesis, Spectroscopic Characterizations, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulations, and Comprehensive DFT Calculations of Novel Tetrazole 1,5 and 2,5-Disubstituted Tetrazole Scaffolds.
papers.abstract: New 1,5- and 2,5-disubstituted tetrazole derivatives were successfully synthesized under phase-transfer catalysis conditions in good to excellent yields (21%-97%). The structures of the obtained compounds were confirmed by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, as well as single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Density functional theory calculations performed at the B3LYP/DNP 3.5 level showed that compound F possesses the smallest HOMO-LUMO energy gap (3.390 eV), suggesting enhanced chemical reactivity. Monte Carlo/SAA simulations demonstrated strong adsorption tendencies on metallic surfaces, partic
papers.summary: This paper describes the synthesis of novel 1,5- and 2,5-disubstituted tetrazole derivatives using phase-transfer catalysis, with structural confirmation via NMR and X-ray crystallography. DFT calculations identified a lead compound with a small HOMO-LUMO gap indicating high reactivity, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested strong surface adsorption, pointing to potential applications in corrosion inhibition or materials science.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Peptides Trigger Nociceptive Responses Through Spinal TLR4 Pathways.
papers.abstract: Pain is a common neurological manifestation of COVID-19, yet the mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 spike protein fragments contribute to nociceptive processing remain poorly understood. We investigated whether spike-derived peptides directly activate spinal neuroimmune pathways involved in pain signalling.
papers.summary: This study investigates how fragments of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein may directly trigger pain signaling in the spinal cord. The findings suggest that spike peptides activate nociceptive responses through TLR4-mediated neuroimmune pathways, providing a potential mechanism for pain symptoms in COVID-19.

papers.title: Integrative GC-MS, FT-IR, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Drimycarpus racemosus (Roxb.) Hook.f ex Marchand: In Vivo Analgesic and Antidiabetic Potential.
papers.abstract: Traditional medicine has long utilized Drimycarpus racemosus (Roxb.) Hook.f ex Marchand, which is a member of the Anacardiaceae family, to treat inflammation, pain, and metabolic disorders; however, its therapeutic properties have not been experimentally investigated. This study aimed to investigate the analgesic and hypoglycemic activities of D. racemosus leaf extract and explore its bioactive constituents through a computational approach. The most prevalent chemicals found in the plant methanolic extract, according to GC-MS analysis, were Furfural, 4-methoxybenzoic acid, methyl ester and β-s
papers.summary: This study experimentally validates the analgesic and antidiabetic potential of Drimycarpus racemosus leaf extract, supporting its traditional medicinal use. Using GC-MS and FT-IR to identify bioactive compounds and molecular docking to predict their interactions, the authors provide preliminary evidence for the plant's therapeutic effects, though the mechanisms remain to be fully characterized.

papers.title: Exploration of the Potential Mechanisms of Anaphalis virgata Extract in Treating Diabetic Hepatic Injury Based on Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Diabetic hepatic injury is a common complication of diabetes, yet it is often neglected due to its subtle early symptoms. This study explored the effect and mechanism of Anaphalis virgata extract (AVE) in treating diabetic hepatic injury. Serum-exposed components of AVE were identified by LC-MS and used for network pharmacology to predict therapeutic targets and pathways. AVE was evaluated in diabetic rats treated intragastrically at 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg for 10 weeks. Hepatic biochemical parameters were measured, and mechanisms were verified by molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, ELISA, and
papers.summary: This study investigates the therapeutic potential of Anaphalis virgata extract (AVE) against diabetic hepatic injury using network pharmacology and experimental validation. The authors identify serum-exposed components via LC-MS, predict targets and pathways, and confirm protective effects in diabetic rats, with mechanisms verified through molecular dynamics simulation and biochemical assays.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Material Basis of Pogostemon cablin Aqueous Extract: Integrating Zebrafish Modeling, Network Pharmacology, and Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the anti-inflammatory effects of the aqueous extract of Pogostemon cablin and map the network of its main active ingredients, key targets, and signaling pathways. The chemical components of the extract were analyzed via ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q/TOF-MS), and its anti-inflammatory activity was verified using a zebrafish model. The target sites and signaling pathways of these chemical components were identified through bioinformatics analysis, while molecular interactions were simulated
papers.summary: This study identifies the anti-inflammatory components of Pogostemon cablin aqueous extract using UPLC-Q/TOF-MS, validates activity in a zebrafish model, and maps the compound-target-pathway network via network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations. The work provides a systematic approach to understanding the material basis of this herbal medicine's anti-inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Manufacturing and electrostatic surface optimization of CAR-T cells improve therapeutic efficacy in liver malignancies.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has achieved remarkable success in hematologic malignancies, yet demonstrates limited efficacy in solid tumors, including hepatic cancers. T-cell exhaustion and insufficient persistence represent major obstacles. We hypothesized that optimizing both manufacturing processes and CAR structural design could reduce exhaustion and enhance therapeutic outcomes in immunocompetent mouse models of primary and metastatic liver malignancies.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that optimizing CAR-T cell manufacturing processes and engineering the electrostatic surface of the CAR construct can reduce T-cell exhaustion and improve persistence, leading to enhanced therapeutic efficacy in immunocompetent mouse models of primary and metastatic liver cancers. The findings suggest that combined manufacturing and structural design improvements may overcome key barriers to CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: RCSB protein data Bank: Next-generation advanced search for exploration of experimental structures and computed structure models.
papers.abstract: The Protein Data Bank (PDB), established in 1971, is the primary global, open-access archive for experimentally determined 3D macromolecular structures (proteins, RNA, DNA). The research-focused RCSB.org web-portal provides access to these data alongside more than one million machine-learning-predicted structure models, greatly expanding the available structural landscape. Rapid growth of both experimental and computational structures has increased the need for powerful yet accessible search tools that serve a broad and diverse scientific community. Herein, we describe a redesigned RCSB Protei
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: This paper describes a redesigned advanced search interface for the RCSB Protein Data Bank, which now integrates both experimental structures and over one million machine-learning-predicted structure models. The new search tools aim to provide powerful yet accessible querying capabilities for a broad scientific community, addressing the challenges posed by the rapid growth of structural data.

papers.title: GC-MS profiling, in vitro antioxidant and toxicity evaluation, and in silico pharmacokinetic and molecular docking prediction of the phytocompounds of Rungia repens (L.) Nees targeting SarA of Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The medicinal plant Rungia repens (L.) Nees (Acanthaceae) is commonly known as kodagasalai in Tamil. It is recognized for its antipyretic, diuretic, anti-inflammatory, and vermifunge properties. The present study is primarily focused on identifying the phytocompounds and evaluating the antioxidant activity and cytotoxicity of R. repens leaf extract. In silico molecular docking studies were performed for SarA, an anti-virulence target of Staphylococcus aureus, and pharmacokinetic prediction was carried out to identify a suitable compound for drug delivery. The total flavonoid (TFC), phenolic co
papers.summary: This study profiles the phytochemicals in Rungia repens leaf extract using GC-MS, evaluates its antioxidant activity and toxicity, and uses molecular docking to identify compounds that may target the SarA virulence protein of Staphylococcus aureus. The findings suggest that certain phytocompounds have promising antioxidant and anti-virulence potential, with favorable pharmacokinetic properties for drug development.

papers.title: Integrated in Silico and in Vitro Bioactivity Profiling of Selected South African Plant Constituents Against Carbohydrate-Metabolizing Enzymes for Type 2 Diabetes Therapy.
papers.abstract: The increasing global burden of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and the side effects of conventional drugs have driven the search for natural therapeutic alternatives. This study investigates the antidiabetic potential of South African essential oils - specifically Artemisia afra, Agathosma betulina, and Cymbopogon citratus - which are traditionally used in diabetes treatment but lack comprehensive scientific validation. Using an integrated research framework: mining the phytochemical metabolites of the plant source from Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Database and relevant literat
papers.summary: This study combines computational and experimental approaches to evaluate the antidiabetic potential of compounds from three South African medicinal plants (Artemisia afra, Agathosma betulina, and Cymbopogon citratus) by testing their ability to inhibit carbohydrate-metabolizing enzymes relevant to type 2 diabetes. The integrated in silico and in vitro profiling provides preliminary evidence supporting the traditional use of these plants, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Exploring the Binding Specificity of Siglec-Derived Peptides to Human Primary Amine Oxidase Using an Integrative Approach to Ligand Epitope Mapping.
papers.abstract: Human primary amine oxidase (AOC3) is a membrane-anchored protein expressed on the luminal surface of the vascular endothelium at sites of inflammation. It binds via protein-protein interactions to the CE-loops of the C22 domain in Siglec-9 and Siglec-10, but the exact mechanism of interaction is unknown on an atomic level. The AOC3 binding to a radiolabeled Siglec-9 peptide can be used to image inflammation by positron emission tomography (PET). In the present study, a combination of computational and wet lab experiments is used to map the binding of the original and designed shorter Siglec-d
papers.summary: This study combines computational modeling with wet-lab experiments to map how Siglec-derived peptides bind to human primary amine oxidase (AOC3), a protein involved in inflammation. The authors identify key binding epitopes and design shorter peptides that retain binding affinity, which could improve PET imaging of inflammation. The work provides atomic-level insights into the interaction mechanism and offers a rational basis for developing better imaging probes.

papers.title: A novel heterozygous splicing variant in the EIF4ENIF1 gene in a family with premature ovarian insufficiency and early menopause.
papers.abstract: Female reproductive aging is a continuum characterized by the depletion of ovarian follicles, including Early Menopause (EM) and Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI).POI exhibits a strong genetic predisposition. Eukaryotic Translation Initiation Factor 4E nuclear import factor 1 (EIF4ENIF1), a key regulator of gene expression, plays a crucial role in oocyte maturation and follicular development. Accumulating evidence indicates that functional abnormalities in EIF4ENIF1 are closely associated with the onset and progression of POI. Therefore, identifying pathogenic variants in EIF4ENIF1 is of s
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel heterozygous splicing variant in the EIF4ENIF1 gene in a family affected by premature ovarian insufficiency and early menopause, adding to the evidence that EIF4ENIF1 dysfunction contributes to ovarian aging. The finding expands the genetic spectrum of POI and may aid in genetic counseling and diagnosis.

papers.title: Analysing open-source protein folding models for nanobody binding prediction.
papers.abstract: Antibody-based therapeutics are a rapidly expanding class of treatments, with over 200 approved candidates and thousands in clinical trials. Computational pre-filtering using protein structure prediction models has the potential to reduce the cost of wet-lab screening, yet the relationship between model confidence measures and functional binding properties remains incompletely understood. Here, we evaluate whether confidence measures produced by contemporary open-source protein structure prediction models are suitable for in silico screening of nanobody-antigen interactions.
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether confidence scores from open-source protein structure prediction models can be used to computationally screen nanobody-antigen interactions, potentially reducing the need for costly wet-lab experiments. The authors assess the relationship between model confidence measures and functional binding properties, providing insights into the utility of these models for antibody-based therapeutic development.

papers.title: Research on the influence of bisphenol A on precocious puberty based on network toxicology and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Precocious puberty (PP) is a pediatric endocrine disorder. Bisphenol A (BPA) is an endocrine disruptor. This study aimed to computationally investigate BPA-associated PP targets and mechanisms via network toxicology and molecular dynamics.
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods, including network toxicology and molecular dynamics simulations, to investigate how bisphenol A (BPA), an endocrine disruptor, may contribute to precocious puberty (PP). The authors identify potential BPA-related targets and pathways involved in PP, providing a mechanistic hypothesis for BPA's role in this condition.

papers.title: Fumarate-associated immunometabolic network in Periodontitis revealed by integrated transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a long-term inflammatory disease of the gums that damages the tissues and bone supporting the teeth. Recent studies suggest that changes in cellular metabolism may influence immune responses during chronic inflammation; however, the contribution of fumarate-associated transcriptional programs to periodontitis remains unclear. In this study, we integrated bulk transcriptomic data from human periodontal tissues with single-cell RNA sequencing data to identify fumarate-associated genes and cell clusters associated with periodontitis. Our analyses revealed a fumarate-associated im
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data from human periodontal tissues to identify fumarate-associated genes and cell clusters linked to periodontitis. The findings reveal a fumarate-associated immunometabolic network that may contribute to chronic inflammation, offering new insights into the metabolic regulation of immune responses in periodontal disease.

papers.title: Heteroleptic Metal Complexes of 4-(2-Pyridylazo)resorcinol and 1,10-Phenanthroline: Synthesis, Comprehensive Characterization, Electrochemical and Antioxidant Properties, and Computational Investigations.
papers.abstract: New heteroligand metal complexes, [M(phen) (PAR) (OAc)]·H2O (M = Mn(II) (1), Cu(II) (3)) and [Co(phen) (PAR) (H2O)]OAc·H2O (2), incorporating 4-(2-pyridylazo)resorcinol (PAR) as the primary ligand and 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) as the secondary ligand, were synthesized and comprehensively characterized. Elemental analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, thermal analysis, magnetic susceptibility measurements, and molar conductivity studies confirmed the proposed compositions and coordination modes of the complexes. Spectroscopic data revealed that PAR coordinates to the metal center in its deprotonated fo
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of new heteroleptic metal complexes containing 4-(2-pyridylazo)resorcinol and 1,10-phenanthroline, with detailed analysis of their electrochemical and antioxidant properties. The study provides foundational data on the coordination chemistry and potential bioactivity of these complexes, though it is primarily a synthetic and characterization work with limited direct biological application.

papers.title: The "two flowers therapy": clinical efficacy and mechanisms of a total glucosides of paeony -colchicine dual-drugs for Behçet's disease derived from Chinese physicians' medication experience.
papers.abstract: To elucidate the synergistic mechanism of "Two flowers therapy" - a Behçet's disease (BD) treatment regimen used in China for more than 30 years, namely Total Glucosides of Paeony (TGP)-colchicine - and its efficacy, safety in BD with mucocutaneous involvement.
papers.summary: This study evaluates the 'Two flowers therapy' (Total Glucosides of Paeony combined with colchicine), a Chinese treatment for Behçet's disease with mucocutaneous involvement, and explores its synergistic mechanism. The findings support its clinical efficacy and safety, and suggest a mechanistic basis for the combination.

papers.title: Aegeline mitigates isoproterenol-induced myocardial infarction: insights from biochemical, histopathological, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although considerable advances have been made in its diagnosis and management, the development of safe and effective cardioprotective agents remains an active area of investigation. Natural products continue to attract interest as potential therapeutic candidates because of their diverse pharmacological activities. Aegeline, an alkaloidal amide isolated from Aegle marmelos, has demonstrated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its cardioprotective effects in experimental myocardial injury h
papers.summary: This study investigates the cardioprotective potential of aegeline, a natural compound from Aegle marmelos, in a rat model of isoproterenol-induced myocardial infarction. The results show that aegeline treatment reduces cardiac damage, as evidenced by improved biochemical markers and histopathological outcomes, and in silico analyses suggest it may act through anti-inflammatory and antioxidant pathways. The findings support aegeline as a promising candidate for further development as a cardioprotective agent.

papers.title: FAERS-based pharmacovigilance and network toxicology analysis of esomeprazole-associated osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a progressive skeletal disorder often exacerbated by pharmacological agents. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), particularly esomeprazole, have been epidemiologically linked to OP, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses FAERS pharmacovigilance data and network toxicology to investigate the association between esomeprazole and osteoporosis, confirming a significant signal and identifying potential molecular mechanisms. The findings provide evidence for esomeprazole's role in osteoporosis risk and highlight key targets and pathways, though the exact mechanisms require further validation.

papers.title: The Redesign of the Molecular Scaffold of Viral Ion Channel Blockers.
papers.abstract: The rise of rapidly mutating viruses poses growing challenges for drug developers in the fight against antiviral resistance. Viral ion channels generally have low mutation rates and are therefore considered emerging targets for a sustainable solution to the problem of resistance. This study reports the redesign of scaffolds for drug candidates targeting viral ion channels. The redesign was powered by a combination of a computational docking protocol that accounts for water molecules (HydroDock) and a subsequent quantum mechanics-based scoring (QMH-L) of the drug candidates. Extending the antiv
papers.summary: This study reports the redesign of molecular scaffolds for drug candidates targeting viral ion channels, which are attractive antiviral targets due to their low mutation rates. The redesign was powered by a computational docking protocol that accounts for water molecules (HydroDock) combined with quantum mechanics-based scoring (QMH-L), offering a potential sustainable approach to combat antiviral resistance.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 NSP8-Derived Peptide Effectively Suppresses the Activity of Helicase NSP13.
papers.abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) nonstructural protein 13 (NSP13) is a multifunctional helicase that plays a central role in viral RNA replication and suppression of host innate immunity. Beyond its essential function within the replication-transcription complex (RTC), NSP13 antagonizes type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling through interaction with the host kinase TBK1, making its protein-protein interactions attractive antiviral targets. In this study, we investigated whether fragments derived from the viral cofactor NSP8 can competitively interfere with NSP13 intera
papers.summary: This study identifies a peptide derived from SARS-CoV-2 NSP8 that can inhibit the helicase activity of NSP13, a key viral protein involved in RNA replication and immune evasion. The peptide likely disrupts NSP13's interactions, offering a potential new antiviral strategy against COVID-19.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning, deep learning, and docking to predict aristolochic acid A carcinogenesis.
papers.abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms of renal clear cell carcinoma (RCC) induced by Aristolochic acid A (AAA) using machine learning, deep learning, and molecular docking approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning, deep learning, and molecular docking to investigate how aristolochic acid A (AAA) may cause renal clear cell carcinoma, identifying potential molecular mechanisms and targets. It provides a computational framework for predicting carcinogenesis and could inform risk assessment and drug development.

papers.title: CCR1-mediated monocyte chemotaxis in the immunopathology of primary Sjögren's syndrome: multi-omics integration analysis and computational target prioritization implicating Polygonatum odoratum.
papers.abstract: Primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease with no specific etiological treatment. Polygonatum odoratum, a traditional yin-nourishing herb, is used in treating pSS, but its molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the potential association of CCR1 with pSS immunopathology and to computationally assess its candidacy as a predicted target of P. odoratum.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics integration and computational target prioritization to implicate CCR1-mediated monocyte chemotaxis in primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) immunopathology, and predicts the herb Polygonatum odoratum may act on CCR1 as a therapeutic target. The findings suggest a potential molecular mechanism for this traditional herb in pSS treatment, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular modelling analysis of Arctium lappa phytochemicals in valproic acid-induced hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Valproic acid (VPA) is an antiepileptic drug commonly employed to treat epilepsy. Despite this, the clinical application of VPA is often hindered by adverse reactions. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals obtained from Arctium lappa to mitigate VPA-induced toxicity and to determine the mechanisms involved.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate whether phytochemicals from Arctium lappa (greater burdock) can counteract liver and pancreatic toxicity caused by the antiepileptic drug valproic acid. The analysis identifies key compounds and their potential protein targets, suggesting a mechanistic basis for their protective effects.

papers.title: Integrative Multiomics Analysis Reveals a Cancer Stem Cell-Driven Prognostic Signature and Nominates Belinostat for Targeted Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) suffers from a poor prognosis largely due to its profound molecular heterogeneity and high frequency of relapse, challenges that are closely linked to the biology of cancer stem cells (CSCs) and a lack of effective stemness-related prognostic biomarkers. Identifying CSC-related prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets is critical for improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multiomics analysis to identify a cancer stem cell (CSC)-driven prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and nominates the drug belinostat as a potential targeted therapy. The findings provide new biomarkers and a therapeutic candidate that could improve patient stratification and treatment outcomes.

papers.title: Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre leaf extract: in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches to combat the waterborne bacterial pathogens associated with diarrheal conditions.
papers.abstract: Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre, a medicinal plant traditionally used in Indian ethnomedicine, was evaluated for its antidiarrheal, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties through a combination of in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. This study aims to study the traditional use of plants in medicine and identify a suitable secondary metabolite that can help reduce bacterial growth in living systems, thereby lowering the risk of waterborne diseases and diarrhea. Screening of P. pinnata leaf extract confirmed the presence of various bioactive classes, including alkaloids, flavonoids, etc.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates the medicinal plant Pongamia pinnata for its ability to combat waterborne bacterial pathogens associated with diarrhea, using laboratory, animal, and computational methods. The leaf extract showed antibacterial and antioxidant properties, supporting its traditional use and identifying potential bioactive compounds for drug development.

papers.title: An NRIP1-Centric Monocyte Immunogenetic Bridge Between Heart Failure and Ischemic Stroke.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) and ischemic stroke (IS) frequently co-occur and worsen each other. Circulating immune cells may act as a cross-organ inflammatory bridge, but the key immune lineage, genetically supported mediators, and druggable targets remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study identifies a monocyte-centered immunogenetic link between heart failure and ischemic stroke, highlighting NRIP1 as a key regulatory gene. The findings suggest that NRIP1-mediated inflammatory pathways in monocytes may serve as a druggable target to address the comorbidity of these two conditions.

papers.title: Multifunctional nanozyme platforms in central nervous system therapies: from rational design to translational medicine.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders-including ischemic stroke, traumatic brain/spinal cord injury, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease-have long faced limitations in achieving functional recovery and disease-modifying therapies because of their complex pathophysiological mechanisms. Traditional therapies are often constrained by poor penetration across CNS barriers, limited participation in multiple pathological cascades, and insufficient persistence of therapeutic effects. Nanozymes are a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-like catalytic activity and tunable physicochemical proper
papers.summary: This review discusses the design and application of multifunctional nanozymes—nanomaterials with enzyme-like catalytic activity—for treating central nervous system disorders such as stroke, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's. It highlights how nanozymes can overcome limitations of traditional therapies by crossing CNS barriers and targeting multiple pathological pathways, and it outlines challenges and prospects for clinical translation.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microecological characteristics associated with tobacco root-knot nematode disease.
papers.abstract: Root-knot nematode disease poses a serious threat to the production of tobacco and other crops, but the rhizosphere microecological response mechanisms during disease development remain unclear. In this study, we collected rhizosphere soil from healthy and diseased tobacco plants in typical tobacco-growing areas of Kunming, Yunnan Province, China, and we systematically identified the differences in soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, and the microbial community composition and structure based on 16S rDNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Compared to healthy rhizosphere soil, disease
papers.summary: This study compares rhizosphere soil from healthy and root-knot nematode-diseased tobacco plants, identifying differences in soil properties, enzyme activities, and microbial community composition using 16S rDNA and ITS sequencing. The findings reveal distinct microecological shifts associated with disease, providing insights into the rhizosphere response mechanisms to nematode infection.

papers.title: Bacteriophage lysins: a promising strategy for combating foodborne pathogens in food safety.
papers.abstract: Food safety is a major public concern, with foodborne pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium perfringens, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus causing millions of infections and significant economic losses annually. Phage and endolysin therapies have emerged as promising environmentally friendly strategies for pathogen control. Bacteriophage lytic enzymes, which are proteins produced during the late stage of phage infection, offer advantages over whole phages, including rapid bactericidal action, a broad antibacterial spectrum, and a low risk of inducing resistance
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of bacteriophage lysins (endolysins) as a promising strategy to combat foodborne pathogens in food safety. It highlights their advantages over whole phages, including rapid bactericidal action, broad spectrum, and low resistance risk, positioning them as an environmentally friendly alternative for pathogen control.

papers.title: Licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants: structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The development of innovative vaccine platforms, including protein subunit and nucleic acid vaccines, has advanced rapidly and established new technical paradigms for infectious disease prophylaxis. Nonetheless, many next-generation vaccines display suboptimal intrinsic immunogenicity owing to restricted antigenic complexity, resulting in inadequate protective immunity when delivered without adjuvants. Aluminum-containing adjuvants, the most widely deployed clinical adjuvants, primarily potentiate humoral immunity but elicit modest cellular immune responses, thereby failing to satisfy the immu
papers.summary: This review examines licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants, focusing on their structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions. It highlights the limitations of current aluminum-based adjuvants in inducing cellular immunity and discusses how TLR4 agonists can enhance both humoral and cellular responses for next-generation vaccines.

papers.title: Theta-Defensin Proteins: Conformational Variability and Environmental Effects.
papers.abstract: Theta-defensins are a unique class of cyclic antimicrobial peptides known for their exceptional structural stability and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. Despite their therapeutic potential in mammals, the effects of solvent environments and specific mutations on their conformational stability remain poorly understood. This paper employs all-atom molecular dynamics simulations under different solvent conditions to investigate the structural dynamics of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2) peptides, as well as solvent effects. BTD-2 was selected due to its higher arginine content, enhancing it
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to explore how solvent conditions and mutations affect the conformational stability of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2), a cyclic antimicrobial peptide. The findings reveal that environmental factors and specific sequence changes can significantly influence the peptide's structural dynamics, providing insights for engineering more stable therapeutic peptides.
